title: Wiha Voltage Tester AC 120-250V $14.96 + Delivery ($0 In-Store) @ PCA Electrical Supplies (Price Beat $13.46 @ Bunnings)
body:
Deal: Wiha Voltage Tester AC 120-250V $14.96 + Delivery ($0 In-Store) @ PCA Electrical Supplies (Price Beat $13.46 @ Bunnings)

[M00Cow] limited voltage range, why would you buy this over a $10 2pack on Amazon?
or a multimeter?
https://www.bunnings.com.au/click-hobbyist-multimeter_p03810…
[slipperypete] lol did you see the reviews for the Bunnings one. Good enough reason right there
limited voltage range
It's designed for a specific use. I'm not overly keen on these, much prefer a non contact device but it's a good price for a good brand
[M00Cow] when I posted my comment the Subject said
Wiha Voltage Tester AC 220-250V
hence my
limited voltage range
No I didn't read, nor take much stock in Bunnings reviews. But relying on a single voltage probe isn't ideal, hence why I suggested a multimeter. I've got a 40yo Fluke, does 500v ac/dc/ohms/diode.
But any reason why this is better then the similar Amazon stuff?
[slipperypete] which Amazon stuff are you referring to? Makes it hard without an example
This isn't a multimeter, as I said, it has different uses. This is a prod and test device that fits in your pocket. It costs $15. It lights up when domestic voltages are detected
[cornflakes] Oh boy, DIY electrical. Time to get the popcorn out.
[M00Cow] meh, most other countries allow DIY electrical,.the ETU are big Labor donors to.keep their monopoly. Domestic is 3 wires, we're not talking complicated stuff.
I suspect this is to make sure you've got the power/fuse/etc off. I still.prefer a multimeter.
[bboz] Agree. It's a BS rort here in Aus. In NZ, you can do you own work and then get an electrician to check it and sign off. I think that is a great compromise.
[slipperypete] You should shop local
378 Parramatta Road. How far away is acceptable?
[Frozensage] this or that voltage tester thing for $28 from klein?
[Horacio] ooo, link? I do have a cheap no-name non-contact tester that seems to work fine but might be nice to have one of those
[Quarn] Just get a none contact probe, no risk and easier to use.
